name: Code Slots
description: A one-time code input; each digit springs into its own slot, an error empties the slots from last to first, and success draws a curtain with a tick rising in the middle.
interactionNotes: Click the row and type digits; each digit springs into the next slot. You can also paste the whole code at once — the digits settle in a cascade. When the last slot fills, `onComplete` is called and whatever decision you made about the code plays out: acceptance opens an accent curtain from the middle with a tick rising, rejection empties the slots from last to first and then clears the code. The component does not decide whether the code is correct — that is your job.

props.name: length
props.description: Number of slots.

props.name: value
props.description: The controlled code. A digit arriving from outside settles in with a cascade, and a digit that leaves empties its slot.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial uncontrolled code; it renders already settled from the start.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called on every edit — including clearing at the end of a rejection.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Once, when the last slot fills.

props.name: status
props.description: Error empties the slots from last to first under a danger tint and clears the code; success merges the fills into a curtain and locks the input.

props.name: mask
props.description: Shows a dot in place of each digit.

props.name: caret
props.description: Blinking caret in the active slot.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the row and ignores input.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Focuses the input on mount.

props.name: accentColor
props.description: Fill of a settled digit, the ring of the active slot, and the success curtain.

props.name: inkColor
props.description: The caret, and the tint of the active slot.

props.name: slotColor
props.description: Surface of an empty slot.

props.name: digitColor
props.description: Color of the digit on the fill.

props.name: dangerColor
props.description: Ring and fill color in the error state.

props.name: slotSize
props.description: Slot width, px. Height and digit size follow it too.

props.name: gap
props.description: Spacing between slots, px.

props.name: radius
props.description: Corner rounding, px; capped at half the slot size.

props.name: bounce
props.description: Spring bounce of settling; zero means damped with no bounce.

props.name: settle
props.description: Seconds a digit takes to settle or empty.

props.name: rise
props.description: Pixels a digit rises from below; zero means it only fades.

props.name: cascade
props.description: Milliseconds between slots when several settle together or empty in a rejection.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the input.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class for the root.

tips: This component does not decide whether the code is correct — you know where the right code lives. Take `onComplete` and set `status` after the server responds.
Pasting works: copy the whole code and paste it onto the row, and the digits settle in a cascade. The SMS keyboard autofill (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`) is wired up too.
Persian input is accepted too — both Persian and Arabic-Indic digit forms convert to the same Latin code. The `value` and `onChange` values are always Latin, because that is data, not display.
Filled slots are distinguishable from empty ones but **cannot be skipped**: clicking any slot moves the caret to the first empty slot and no further.
Set `cascade` to zero so all digits settle at once; raise it to make the stepped line more obvious. Above 40ms it feels slow on a six-digit code.

This component **does not mirror for right-to-left**, and that is intentional: its geometry is physical (the caret moves via `translateX` and a tap is mapped to a slot via `clientX`). Only the text and digits are Persian — the same rule as `jelly-radio`.

To let the user know you rejected a wrong code, set `status` to `error` and **then yourself** return it to `idle` once the emptying finishes — at the end the component fires `onChange('')`, which is the signal that it is done.
